headline: Tidal Rush: a jetski slalom where the physics and the pixels ride one sea
lede: Rung 1 of #3104, merge pending CI as this report posts; live URL confirmed on the issue when static clears. A Wave Race 64-style slalom — red buoys right, yellow left — on one analytic Gerstner swell table that drives both the vertex shader and the hull, so the sea you see is provably the sea you ride. Three laps of Sunny Bay against two seeded CPU skis, sprint boosts on clean passes, 360s off kickers.

notes.text: TIDAL RUSH at (private until promotion) /retrogames/tidal-rush (private until promoted) — gates, boosts, tricks, two rivals, MODERN sun-glitter sea on a phone budget (no shadow maps, DPR capped).

water.js is the single surface of truth: heightAt/surfaceVy float the hull, waterGLSL() emits the same constants into the shader, and tidalcheck parses both to pin the parity — drawn sea ≡ ridden sea.
tidalcheck joined CI static (24 pins); the red-side mutant goes 21/24 red — the check can fail. Browser drive 10/10, contractcheck 15/15.
#3104 stays open for rung 2: a storm bay whose swell re-rolls every lap. Honest gaps listed in the game README.
